resources.string: Works only in the YouTube app. It presses Back when a Short or the Shorts tab opens, hides Shorts rows once you stop scrolling and, if you choose, covers the Home and Subscriptions feeds. Other apps are ignored (it only notices when YouTube goes to the background). It has no internet access.

How to turn it on:
1. Tap “Open Accessibility Settings”.
2. Find “Shorts Blocker” (often under “Downloaded apps” or “Installed apps”) and switch it on.
3. If the switch is greyed out (Android 13+), tap “Open App Info”, then ⋮ (top right) → “Allow restricted settings”, and try step 2 again.
Shorts (closes Shorts; hides Shorts rows after 3 s without scrolling)
Ticked feeds are covered with a blank panel. Search and the You tab (History, Continue watching, Watch later, playlists) still work.
Debug mode (saves screen info you can share)
✅ The service is turned on in Accessibility settings.
⚠️ The service is OFF. Turn it on in Accessibility settings (steps below).
No internet permission, no analytics, no data collection. Recent activity and screen info stay on your phone unless you share them.
Nothing yet. Open YouTube and come back here.
If something is still visible or acting up: turn on Debug mode, open that screen in YouTube, come back here and tap “Share screen info”.
